name: Aquarium
label: Dischord
lede: A keyboard, a drum kit and a projector loaded with old school films: Aquarium played DC rooms, toured once, made one album, and Dischord put out a two-song 7" in 2009.

eras.title: Songs for the classroom projector
eras.text: Dischord's bio has Jason Hutto and Laura Harris playing instrumentals in front of science films salvaged from Baltimore city schools. Vocals came later, and so did a loyal DC following, though they only ever toured once.

years.h: Two bandmates and a projector full of Baltimore school films
years.p: Keyboardist Jason Hutto, formerly of Motor-Cycle Wars, and drummer Laura Harris start Aquarium in 2001. Their instrumentals play against reels salvaged from Baltimore city schools.
years.xp:
Dischord's bio lists the footage as science classroom fare and nature films. Hutto played electric piano and keyboards, Harris played drums, and at first nobody sang.

Hutto began adding vocals to fill out the sound, and the instrumentals turned into songs. Dischord dates the start to 2001; Wikipedia says 2002.

eras.title: One album, and a last look in the rearview
eras.text: The self-titled album was recorded at Inner Ear with Brendan Canty mixing, and came out in October 2006. Sources put the end of the band in 2006 too, though photos show a duo onstage in 2007.

years.cap: Jason Hutto at the keyboard, Black Cat, Washington DC, September 2, 2006
years.src: Dischord: Aquarium s/t · Wikipedia: The Aquarium
years.h: Dischord No. 155 is 11 songs about living in DC
years.p: Recorded at Inner Ear, mixed by [[Brendan Canty|8b505ef0-c5a7-4deb-bc32-27c882f3c40e]] at Trixie Studios, mastered by TJ Lipple at Silver Sonya. Titles include Can't Afford To Live Here, White House and Channel 9.
years.xp:
Dischord lists the record as recorded in 2006; the October release date comes from Wikipedia.

Canty, the Fugazi drummer, mixed it, which keeps the credits close to the label's own family.

years.cap: Laura Harris on drums and Jason Hutto at the keyboard, Fort Reno, Washington DC, August 2, 2007
years.h: Aquarium end in 2006, per the sources
years.p: Wikipedia gives 2002 to 2006 as the band's run, the same year the album came out. No source says why it ended.
years.xp: The photo here is from Fort Reno in August 2007, and another set shows the duo at the Warehouse Next Door that May. Dates differ by source, so the exact end is still open.

eras.title: A review, a 7", and Harris behind Ex Hex
eras.text: The Washington Post's Express reviewed the album in January 2007. Dischord followed with the two-song Performer 7" in 2009, and Harris later drummed for Ex Hex.

years.cap: The Aquarium at the Warehouse Next Door, Washington DC, May 12, 2007
years.src: Washington Post Express · Wikipedia: The Aquarium
years.h: The Washington Post's Express reviews the new album
years.p: The review runs on January 30, 2007, a few months after the record came out.
years.xp: Wikipedia quotes the Post calling the band's sound "catchy, vibrant, and slightly trippy". The Express page itself wouldn't load here, so only its date and title are confirmed.

years.p: Dischord No. 164 is a two-song 7" released in 2009.
years.xp: It came out three years after the album. Dischord's discography lists it as release 164, with the two songs credited to the Aquarium.

yt: Laura Harris on The Trap Set
years.h: Harris takes the drum stool in Ex Hex
years.p: Laura Harris, who'd also drummed for Benjy Ferree, joins [[Mary Timony|d9c8dc3c-15b8-40d5-8153-ae9214aeef55]]'s trio with Betsy Wright, and later tours with [[Death Valley Girls|987c6ccf-d4c5-4f23-938a-c0a21782803d]].
years.xp: Dischord's bio says Hutto toured with E.D. Sedgwick, played guitar in Motor Cycle Wars and later joined Soccer Team.
